recs.stt: Local-first software: You own your data, in spite of the cloud (2019)
recs.x:
In my experience so far, some things get more complicated when building a local-first application, and some things get a lot easier. What gets easier is that once you've modeled and implemented the data-layer (which does require you to rethink / unlearn a few principles), you don't need to worry about data-fetching, errors etc. as much as in a regular "API-based" app.

Another interesting video I recommend on this topic is about Linear's "Sync Engine" which employs some of the local-first techniques as well: [link]

recs.stt: You don't need a CRDT to build a collaborative experience
recs.x:
You may not need CRDT per-se, but building a collaborative experience is so difficult. I worked on collaborative systems for a bit, and also have read a bit about how Figma and Notion do it (this is a good read: [link] ) -- it's still super hard to get right.

This talk by Karri about Linear's "sync engine" is also a good watch: [link] .
